title: Cooperation in Polygynous Households: Experimental Evidence from Northern Benin
title_zh: 多妻制家庭中的合作：来自贝宁北部的实验证据

abstract: ABSTRACT Given increases in climate change and surface water overallocation pressures in the future, groundwater will play an increasingly important role for water supply. This requires greater investment in water security, with the nature‐based water management tool of managed aquifer recharge (MAR) a cost‐effective alternative to more conventional choices such as dams or desalination. While MAR is a mature and safe technology that has been used for decades around the world, currently there is a lack of private and public sector investment in MAR in Australia. The main barriers to MAR implementation are not hydrogeological, but legislation and policy. Our study investigates MAR policy issues further by undertaking a thematic legislative analysis of 252 Australian state and territory water and environmental legislation and policy documents and conducting a focus group/interview discussion with state/territory MAR policy experts ( n = 18). The legislative review finds that Australian MAR legislation is highly complex, providing no ownership of recovery water nor security from government opportunism, and leads to high regulatory costs, disincentivising private sector investment. The study concludes by providing targeted recommendations to reduce implementation barriers and regulatory and transaction costs through reducing regulatory risk, strengthening property rights, improving regulatory processes and providing better education and guidance.
abstract_zh: 摘要 鉴于未来气候变化及地表水过度分配压力的加剧，地下水在水资源供应中将扮演日益重要的角色。这要求加大对水安全的投资，而基于自然的水管理工具——含水层人工补给（MAR）相较于大坝或海水淡化等传统选择，是一种成本效益更高的替代方案。尽管MAR是一项成熟且安全的技术，已在全球范围内应用数十年，但目前澳大利亚在MAR方面的私人和公共部门投资仍显不足。MAR实施的主要障碍并非水文地质条件，而是立法与政策层面。本研究通过对252项澳大利亚州和领地水资源及环境立法与政策文件进行主题性立法分析，并与州/领地MAR政策专家（n=18）开展焦点小组/访谈讨论，进一步探讨MAR政策问题。立法审查发现，澳大利亚的MAR立法高度复杂，既未明确回收水的所有权，也未提供防范政府机会主义行为的保障，且导致高昂的监管成本，从而抑制了私人部门的投资积极性。研究最后提出了针对性建议，旨在通过降低监管风险、强化产权、改进监管流程及提供更好的教育与指导，减少实施障碍及监管和交易成本。

title: Investigating the Suitability of Managed Aquifer Recharge Legislation Across Australia and Lessons for Reducing Barriers
